localChanges: chore: work towards a 3D map, not offered yet: under ?3d=1 the Riflemen's, Musketmen's and Marines' arms bend smoothly as they raise their weapons, the Marines' hands staying on their rifles (#1370)

log: The same tools/blender/rig.py as models-realistic-cc0's (civ-clone/models-realistic-cc0#27), which fixes civ-clone/models-realistic-cc0#26:
While a hold eases on or off, the holding elbow's bend is eased, and the hand slides along the prop (up to 10 cm, never past its ends) to keep the wrist at that reach.
A slide that would go more than 5 cm in a frame fails the build.
Nothing in this set is rigged yet, so no model changes.

This is the same tools/blender/rig.py and tools/check.py as models-realistic-cc0's (civ-clone/models-realistic-cc0#32). A prop's `slides: false` (a rifle held by its pistol grip) moves it with the hand that holds it as a hold eases, rather than the hand sliding along it. The jerk check measures that move as a vector. Nothing in this set is rigged yet, so no model changes.
The arm holding a rifleman's weapon no longer snaps as he raises and lowers it in a fight (fixes #26).

While a hold eases on or off, tools/blender/rig.py eases the holding elbow's bend from what the keys give to what the full hold needs. The hand slides along the weapon (up to 10 cm, never past its ends) so the wrist sits at that reach. A full hold just out of reach is eased to all the same. A slide that would go more than 5 cm in a frame fails the build.
The Marine now lowers his rifle over 7 frames, against 4 before. The Riflemen, Marines and Musketmen otherwise rebuild as they were outside `fight`, and the Partisan rebuilds unchanged.

Four fresh reviews; their findings are fixed. Raised for later: #28 (the Marine's left elbow), #29 (his hand slides off his pistol grip), #30 (the weapon runs through the fist as it's raised) and #31 (the slide's quiet cases).

The Marine's right hand stays on his rifle's pistol grip as he raises and lowers it (fixes #29). While the hold eases, his rifle moves with the hand rather than sliding through it. A prop says so with `slides: false`, which rig.py and check.py accept.

His left hand comes up to the fore-end as the rifle reaches his shoulder, and leaves it before the rifle's lowered. It no longer reaches out straight-armed and snaps its elbow 25 degrees in one frame (fixes #28). It's keyed where it grips, so it steps at most 8 degrees a frame. Through the burst his right arm, rifle and muzzle are as they were. At each kick, his left elbow sits about 1 cm off where it was, and the hand rolls about 6 degrees.
The jerk check (SLIDE_STEP) measures a moved prop's move as a vector. The Riflemen, Musketmen and Partisans rebuild unchanged. Two fresh reviews; the findings are fixed or on #31.
